To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of fault-tolerant data and compute intensive parallel programs over a network of workstations is comparable to that of non-fault-tolerant programs, and that the performance of such programs can be predicted by analysis of application structure and benchmark measurement of hardware performance".

the measured performance of our fault-tolerant bag-of-tasks implementation is close to the performance predicted by analysis, that performance can be improved by increasing the number of nodes and that the performance of the system is scalable with respect to the number of nodes.
The system described in this paper is well suited to the parallel execution of data- and compute-intensive programs that require persistence and fault tolerance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and applying the techniques for fault-tolerant parallel processing in a distributed system.
the design and implementation of an environment that allows parallel programs to be developed and deployed over a distributed system.
the development and evaluation of a system for the parallel execution of data-intensive applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the system performs as well as a single workstation, and that this is not an unreasonable expectation for a system of this type.
the measured performance of the three applications is in close agreement with the predicted performance, and that the system is well suited to a wide range of applications.
the system performs as well as a comparable system based on a shared memory model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the system is suitable for a wide class and size of application and that the measured performance of the system is in line with the performance that would be expected for a parallel system.
we have developed a fault-tolerable bag of tasks system which is capable of supporting the execution of a range of data and compute-intensive applications over a distributed network of workstations.

the performance of a bag of tasks implementation over a network of workstations is comparable with that of a single workstation, provided that the network is fast enough to support the communication requirements of the application.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of persistent objects and RPC can be used in the implementation of a wide class of fault tolerant parallel programs with a performance that compares well to that of programs implemented using shared memory.
it is feasible to achieve fault tolerance in a distributed environment with a reasonable overhead in performance, and that the overhead is not prohibitive in a wide range of applications.
a system that is designed for a specific class of applications and is implemented with the appropriate level of abstraction, can achieve good performance in practice.
